Name: LIFNano Therapeutics
Description:
It is known that LIF (Leukaemia Inhibitory Factor) is a protein that can enable the repair of damaged neurons, and has promised the possibility of treatment for Multiple Sclerosis and other neurodegenerative diseases. The challenge has always been to find a way to deliver LIF to the precise location of the damaged neurons, and this is the basis of the LIFNano Rx breakthrough. Our research has developed a method of packaging a measured amount of LIF into tiny particles that can be delivered into the bloodstream (via injection or nasal spray), where they will circulate until they reach the blood-brain barrier. A unique antibody coating allows them to pass through this barrier exclusively and, once assembled at the treatment site, the completely inert particles will disintegrate, leaving only the LIF molecules and a small amount of water and carbon dioxide.

The LIFNano Rx system is a very elegant solution to several problems: it enables precise targeting of the treatment area – a more focused and economical approach; and it delivers the treatment in a completely clean, contaminant-free, easily reproducible molecular formula, eliminating the need for expensive and difficult cell-based treatments.

Name: PATROLS
Description:
Exposure to engineered nanomaterials (ENM) poses a risk to human and environmental health. However, at present, the test methods used to assess this risk are inadequate and unrealistic. Current test systems utilise scientific models that lack the detail and complexity of the environment and the human body, and only consider the effects of short-term ENM exposure which does not reflect realistic extended or repeated exposure scenarios. 
The primary aim of PATROLS is therefore to establish and standardise a set of innovative, next generation safety testing tools that more accurately predict adverse effects caused by long-term ENM exposure in humans and the environment. PATROLS will achieve its aim by: 
•	Producing realistic and predictive cultured 3D tissue models of the lung, gastrointestinal tract and liver for ENM safety assessment.
•	Developing innovative methods for safety assessment in ecologically relevant test systems and organisms, selected according to their position in the food chain
•	Characterising ENM under relevant experimental conditions dictated by the advanced human and environmental models developed.
•	Creating robust computational methods for ENM exposure, dose modelling and hazard prediction.
The cutting-edge models, hazard reporter tests and computational methods developed through PATROLS will allow ENM to be categorised based on their human and environmental risk. The improved predictivity of the tools generated will help to minimise uncertainty in ENM safety, thereby reducing the extent of animal testing in current use. Furthermore, the PATROLS toolbox   will provide effective data to support and enhance the current ENM safety evaluation frameworks.

Name: PERSEUS EU Project
Description:
PERSEUS is an EU-funded research project pioneering a nanotechnology-based cancer treatment for deep-seated, drug-resistant, and metastatic tumours.

Nanotechnology in cancer care is still in its infancy, but PERSEUS aims to bridge this gap with specially engineered nano-systems made of multifunctional 2D layered nanocrystals. Activated by X-rays, these nanosystems are designed to provide multimodal therapy with minimal side effects. Instead of killing cancer cells directly, CT scanner X-rays trigger and image the nanosystems, which locally produce non-mutagenic oncolytic effects.

This process converts low-energy CT X-rays into reactive oxygen species, radiosensitising agents, and heat; it can also induce immunogenic cell death, exposing or releasing neo-antigens that trigger an anti-cancer immune response. Unlike visible or near-infrared light-based therapies, X-rays can penetrate and treat deep-seated tumours. In short, CT radiation acts as the spark that lights the match – a radical vision for an ambitious, high-risk project.

PERSEUS targets multiple cancers, including metastatic triple negative breast cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The nanosystems are biocompatible and inactive without CT radiation: they only activate where the CT beam is delivered, minimising side effects at distal sites.

The therapy is agnostic with respect to tumour type and gender incidence, since it is not affected by patient biochemistry – a second paradigm shift. PERSEUS unites physicists, chemists, engineers, biologists, physicians, pharmacologists, and radiologists to deliver a transformative nanotechnological approach to urgent, unmet clinical needs.

Name: NanoSpire Inc.
Description:
NanoSpire’s business and technology focus is the harnessing of high speed liquid cavitation reentrant microjets. NanoSpire’s technology is based on cavitation, a boiling phenomenon that involves a change of phase from the liquid to the gaseous state of a particular substance. A laser, ultrasound or other energy source is used to create small high-energy vapor bubbles through phase transition. The collapse of cavitation bubbles in close proximity to a wall generates supersonic liquid microjets naturally pointed towards a wall or other restriction to the collapse of the bubble.

NanoSpire’s patented methods build on, but go beyond the energetic process seen in nature. The size, strength and direction of cavitation reentrant microjets can be controlled by our patented methods to a very high degree of accuracy. Cavitation microjets can travel at up to Mach 4 and are capable of drilling a hole as small as a few nanometers in a diamond. Multiple controlled bubbles are also possible allowing lines to be machined as well as other form factors and machining applications. Cavitation allows a high aspect ratio machining to be obtained and is very repeatable. The technology can mill materials ranging from as soft as plastic to as hard as diamond. The technology can reach across numerous markets including many applications in the membrane/sensor area, (healthcare, automotive, aerospace, etc.), fuel cells, semiconductors, MEMS/NEMS, biotech, microfluidics, instruments and microsurgery markets, among others.

Name: NanoCommons
Description:
Read-across approaches, which are currently absent for NMs, in large part as a result of data fragmentation and inaccessibility, would reduce the cost of nanosafety research and regulation dramatically by removing the need for extensive laboratory and animal testing.

The availability of a nanosafety knowledge infrastructure, that organises and visualises data and data relationships, makes it accessible, integrates computational tools for risk assessment and decision support, enables their validation and facilitates the necessary grouping will be a critical factor in reducing regulatory costs.

The H2020 Infrastructures project, NanoCommons, addresses this gap by creating a community framework and infrastructure for reproducible science, and in particular in silico workflows for nanomaterials and beyond, by:

(i) integration and federation of existing NMs characterisation and interaction mechanisms for knowledge, protocols and data (beyond simple toxicity), along with quality assurance criteria and underpinning ontologies

(ii) compilation, development and expert support of computational tools for mechanistic and statistical modelling, read-across, grouping, safe-by-design and life cycle assessment to the broader user community, and benchmarking of their predictive power; and

(iii) provision of (remote) access to its KnowledgeBase, modelling toolbox and workflow optimisation and supporting expertise to facilitate commercialisation of nanotechnology-derived products.

In any case, cross-field (academia, industry, regulatory) collaboration and voluntary knowledge exchange is needed to promote nanosafety research and create a successful scientific environment.

Name: TECHNO-CLS Project
Description: TECHNO-CLS project aims at the breakthrough in technologies needed for designing and practical realisation of novel gamma-ray Light Sources (LS) operating at photon energies from keV up to GeV range that can be constructed through exposure of oriented crystals (linear, bent and periodically bent) to the beams of ultra-relativistic charged particles. The TECHNO-CLS high-risk/high-gain science-towards-technology breakthrough research programme will address the physics of the processes accompanying the oriented crystal exposure to irradiation by the high-energy electron and positron beams at the atomistic level of detail needed for the realisation of the TECHNO-CLS goals. A broad interdisciplinary, international collaboration has been created previously in the frame of FP7 and H2020 projects, which performed initial experimental tests to demonstrate the crystalline undulator (CU) idea, production and characterisation of periodically bent crystals and the related theory. Additionally, by means of a pre-bunched beam a CU LS has a potential to generate coherent superradiant radiation with wavelengths orders of magnitudes less than 1 Angstrom, i.e. within the range that cannot be reached in existing LSs based on magnetic undulators. Such LSs will have many applications in the basic sciences including nuclear and solid-state physics and the life sciences. Theoretical, computational, experimental and technological results obtained in the course of this project will pave a way for key technological developments of the LSs and their wide exploitation. The TECHNO-CLS international collaboration possesses all the necessary expertise to successfully conduct the outlined programme.

Name: NanoFab Research Project
Description:
The NanoFab Research Project aims to demonstrate a new sustainable and relatively inexpensive manufacturing process for nanofabrication. 

Semiconductors or “chips” are the core component of all electronic devices. Over a trillion semiconductors are manufactured globally each year. The most advanced are incredibly technically complex: chips the size of a postage stamp can have 60 billion transistors. Once designed, chips need to be manufactured, or ‘fabricated’. This involves the etching and depositing of a design onto a semiconductor ‘wafer’. Often defined by ‘node size’; relating to the distance at which each tiny transistor can be etched between each other onto a chip. Fabrication is reliant on specialist materials and equipment including high purity wafers and powerful short wavelength lithography lasers, as well as vacuum sealed clean rooms.

If we could directly write structures at the nanoscale, we would use less precursor, produce less waste and reduce energy consumption and potentially make the process sustainable as well as accessible for smaller manufacturers.

The research team is based at The University of Manchester and includes:

PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR
- Professor David Lewis, Head of the Department of Materials

CO-INVESTIGATORS
- Professor Richard Winpenny, Professor of Inorganic Chemistry, Department of Chemistry
- Dr Jessica Boland, Senior Lecturer of Functional Materials and Devices, Department of Electronic and Electrical Engineering

POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHERS
- Dr Grigore Timco, Department of Materials
- Dr Milad Nonahal, Department of Chemistry

DOCTORAL STUDENT
 - Jacob Young, Department of Materials

PROJECT MANAGER
- Gaynor Spink, School of Natural Sciences, Faculty of Science and Engineering

The University of Manchester received a UKRI, Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council grant (EP/X016404/1) to implement the three-year project which started on 1 May 2023. A no-cost extension has been granted to 30 April 2027.

Nano-manufacturing the materials of tomorrow

The ability to engineer device materials at a sub-100nm scale opens unmatched opportunities to tailor enhanced electrical, optical, magnetic and mechanical properties and functionalities that can be effectively integrated and combined into new form factors and technologies. Inasmuch as integrated circuits and systems shaped our society over the last decades, integrated nanomaterials are set to have revolutionary impact on an ever increasing number of sectors, including information & communication technologies, healthcare, energy conversion and storage, security, transport and environmental technologies. With the size of materials reduced to nm-size scale, their properties not only depend ever more closely on their detailed structure, size, shape and dimensionality but importantly also on their surfaces and interfaces. Much of the new functionality arises from the ability to combine an increasing diversity of materials and achieve greater structural complexity and more complex device architectures. This necessitates new growth and heterogeneous material integration strategies, and for nanomaterials bottom-up or self-assembly approaches are thereby of crucial importance. We investigate crystal growth of nanomaterials that is at the heart of all such emerging technology and is the key future enabler. 

Embedded in Cambridge's strong research community we collaborate with many research groups and industries across the world, bringing our findings to the market through spin-outs (e.g. Abselion) and educating the next generation of nanoscience researchers in the affiliated centre of doctoral training (NanoDTC).

In 1861, James Clerk–Maxwell published Part II of his four-part series "On physical lines of force". In it, he attempted to construct a vortex model of the magnetic field but after much effort neither he, nor other late nineteenth century physicists who followed him, managed to produce a workable theory. What survived from these attempts were Maxwell's four equations of electrodynamics together with the Lorentz force law, formulae that made no attempt to describe an underlying reality but stood only as a mathematical description of the observed phenomena. When the quantum of action was introduced by Planck in 1900 the difficulties that had faced Maxwell's generation were still unresolved. Since then theories of increasing mathematical complexity have been constructed to attempt to bring the totality of phenomena into order with little success. This work examines the problems that had been abandoned long before quantum mechanics was formulated in 1925 and argues that these issues need to be revisited before real progress in the quantum theory of the electromagnetic field can be made.

Readership: Advanced undergraduate and graduate students interested in quantum physics.

Description:
Our mission is to help researchers prepare cleaner, more stable and better-characterised bio-nanoparticle samples for high-performance analytics and functional studies.

Vesiculab products support both extracellular vesicle and synthetic nanomedicine workflows, including EVs, LNPs, liposomes, viral particles and other nanoscale biological systems.

Our solutions are organised across four core categories:

Isolation & purification
Vesi-SEC Micro and Vesi-SEC Midi spin columns enable rapid, gentle and reproducible purification of extracellular vesicles, LNPs and nanomedicines from complex samples. Vesi-Omics kits further support efficient plasma EV isolation by combining ApoB depletion with Vesi-SEC purification.

Labelling
Vesi-Dye LMB provides stable membrane labelling for extracellular vesicles and other lipid-based nanoparticles. When combined with Vesi-SEC Micro, unbound dye and labelling reagents can be efficiently removed to improve specificity and reduce background.

Control & calibration
The Vesi-Ref range of reference materials supports assay standardisation, instrument calibration and cross-platform comparison for single-particle and bulk analytical workflows.

Preservation & storage
Vesi-Safe buffer helps stabilise and preserve extracellular vesicles during dilution, handling, storage and freeze-thaw cycles, supporting consistent recovery and reliable downstream analysis.

Together, Vesiculab solutions help prepare samples for optimal analytics, including flow cytometry, confocal and super-resolution microscopy, fluorescence NTA, SP-IRIS, interferometric light microscopy, mass spectrometry, genomics and transcriptomics.

From discovery research to analytical validation, Vesiculab helps scientists improve reproducibility, standardisation and data quality across extracellular vesicle and nanomedicine research.

nanoXIM•Oral Care: The key hydroxyapatite ingredients for oral care applications, to reduce dental hypersensitivity, enhance enamel remineralization and restore natural whiteness. 
Available in two different forms: water suspension (nano) and powder (micro).

nanoXIM•Medical: Synthetic highly pure hydroxyapatite (HAp) and tricalcium phosphate (TCP) materials for bone regeneration medical devices. 
Available in three different forms: pastes, powders and granules.

nanoXIM•Food: The key hydroxyapatite ingredients for functional food and food supplements, to promote bone strength, reduce bone loss and prevent dental hypersensitivy. 
Available in two different forms: water suspension (nano) and powder (micro).

nanoXIM•Research: Looking for a calcium phosphate for your research? nanoXIM products are also available for several research fields including bio-separation, catalysis, pharma, biotechnology and functionalized textiles.

Name: Molecular Plasma Group
Description:
MPG offers a disruptive Key Enabling Technology (KET) that enables the creation of a wide range of advanced surface functionalities. Examples of what can be achieved using our Molecular Plasma Technology include: adhesion promotion, one-step immobilisation of bio-molecules, virucidal coatings, silicone-free release functionalities, tune-able super-hydrophobicity or hydrophilicity, microfluidic channeling and much more. 

We achieve this by activating a surface and covalently binding the precursor molecules onto the surface using our proprietary Molecular Plasma Process. The outcome is a permanently bonded, custom-designed, nano-metric layer, which features the surface functionality needed by the customer. Our unique technology allows us to work with a wide variety of precursor molecules on basically any kind of surface.

As a full-service provider, we offer application development as well as design, construction and servicing of equipment ranging from lab systems for R&D centers and universities up to industrial in-line systems for continuous production. Our customers are active in a wide range of industries such as fundamental and applied research, aerospace, aeronautics, automotive, packaging, biotechnology, biomedical engineering, micro-electronics, electronics, etc.

Name: NanoSpin
Description:
NanoSpin is a leading designer and manufacturer of top-tier tailor-made electrospinning machines and accessories, specializing in serving the nanotechnology research and engineering community. Our cutting-edge machines are meticulously crafted to meet the unique needs of scientists and engineers in this dynamic field.
At NanoSpin, our foremost commitment is to provide our clients with the most suitable and effective solutions for their research and manufacturing requirements. To achieve this, we offer customizable electrospinning machines that can be tailored to the specific needs of each client. Our product range includes single nozzle, dual nozzle, and Electroblowing systems, providing versatility and flexibility for diverse applications.
We take a customer-centric approach, offering a diverse range of options to suit various requirements. Our product lineup includes Lab-Scale, Pilot, and Industrial machines, along with High Voltage Power supplies, syringe pumps, Collector drums, and Filter tests.

Name: Silicon Microgravity Ltd
Description:
Silicon Microgravity Limited (SMG) is a technology company focused on the inertial navigation and gravity markets.  

Over 10 years of research and development, first at Cambridge University's Nanoscience Department and then carried on inside SMG, has gone in to our resonant MEMS technology.  Today SMG's team of scientists and engineers are based in our Technology Centre in Waterbeach, just north of Cambridge, England.

SMG focuses on two markets.  

> Inertial navigation where our MEMS accelerometers and gyroscopes provide higher accuracy, smaller form factor and lower cost compared to existing sensors.  
> Gravity sensing where our MEMS gravimeters offer robust, compact solutions for gravity surveys and alternative navigation.

Name: Versarien plc
Description: The Versarien Plc group is an advanced engineering materials business developing valuable new materials through the commercialisation of innovative manufacturing processes. The company is a pioneer in the supply of graphene and on course to disrupt a wide variety of industry sectors by producing many proprietary grades of graphene and 2D nanomaterials on a commercial basis. The Group has been at the forefront of developing best-in-class graphene powders and inks, and is the world’s first company to receive full quality assurance certification by the Graphene Council. It has also significantly expanded its graphene manufacturing capabilities around the world to enhance its ability to sustainably produce graphene-based materials to match rising global demand.

Name: Hitachi High-Tech Europe
Description:
Hitachi High-Tech Europe is a market-leading provider of high-tech solutions for industry and academia, covering materials science, life sciences, biotechnology, industrial automation, and nanotechnology.

Our diverse product lineup includes electron microscopes (SEM/TEM/FIB), nano-technology solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, clinical analyzers, biotechnology products and radiation therapy systems. We also provide high value-added solutions to industries fields such as mobility, connectivity, environment and energy. 

Through our core Observation, Measurement, and Analysis technologies, we’re committed to contributing to the realisation of a sustainable society by solving social issues.

Name: Hiden Analytical
Description: Hiden Analytical celebrates more than 40 years of design, development and manufacture of quadrupole mass spectrometers. Our products address a diverse range of applications - precision gas analysis, plasma diagnostics by direct measurement of plasma ions and ion energies, SIMS probes for UHV surface science, catalysis performance quantification, thermo-gravimetric studies - over a pressure range extending from 30 bar processes down to UHV/XHV.

Name: Henniker Plasma
Description:
Henniker Plasma is a leading manufacturer of plasma treatment systems for cleaning, surface activation to improve adhesion, and functional nano-scale coating.

Our innovative plasma treatment equipment is trusted globally in both critical industrial manufacturing settings and by leading academic research groups where it is used in biomedical research, life sciences, energy storage, filtration and many other areas of materials science in general.

Test & Development - We operate extensive laboratory facilities to assess, test and investigate all aspects of plasma surface modification on a wide range of materials.

Driven by expertise - Coupled with extensive in-house and real-world knowledge, we can deliver a tailored treatment to suit your individual product or production needs quickly and efficiently. Our success is built around an exceptional body of knowledge and expertise, backed by highly trained and dedicated staff who understand your application in considerable detail. Our standard configurations cover most applications but we understand too that no two samples or surfaces are the same. That’s why, uniquely, we offer a wide range of options that allow us to customise any standard system for your exact requirements.

Respected by trusted customers - We have worked with some of the most recognisable global brand names and world-leading academic institutes. We work hard to develop long-lasting customer relationships which in turn help us to create the best customer experience possible. Whilst, like many businesses, we measure our success in growth, our core value is developing trust between ourselves and our customers.

Name: Light Trace Photonics
Description:
Detachable fibre-to-chip interconnects for CPO hardware engineering teams.

No micro-optics, no bump-on-carriers, no active alignment, and no epoxy.

Light Trace was founded on deep expertise in integrated quantum photonics where performance and reliability are non-negotiable.

Name: London Centre for Nanotechnology
Description:
The London Centre for Nanotechnology is a UK-based multidisciplinary enterprise operating at the forefront of science and technology. Our purpose is to solve global problems in information processing, healthcare, energy and the environment through the application of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Founded in 2003, the LCN began as a joint venture between University College London and Imperial College London, based at the Bloomsbury and South Kensington sites; from 2018 King's College London joined the collaboration from its base on The Strand.

The LCN occupies a purpose-built eight storey facility in Gordon Street, Bloomsbury (opened in 2006) as well as extensive facilities within different departments at South Kensington and The Strand. The Centre’s experimental research is supported by leading edge modelling, visualisation and theory through its access to state-of-the-art clean-room, characterisation, fabrication, manipulation and design laboratories.

The Centre has a unique operating model that accesses and focusses the combined skills of all three universities across several key departments; Chemistry, Physics, Materials, Medicine, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Biochemical and Biomedical Engineering and Earth Sciences.

The LCN also has strong relationships with the broader nanotechnology and commercial communities and is involved in many major collaborations, nationally and internationally. As the world's only such facility located in the heart of a metropolis, the Centre has superb access to corporate, investment and industrial partners. It is at the forefront of nanotechnology training and enjoys a strong media presence around educating the public and bringing transparency to this far-reaching and emerging science.

Name: IDASONIC Nanocoating & Nanofiber Technologies
Description:
Looking for the right coating and nanofiber technology for your needs?

 Do you need efficiency in energy, precision in medical, and sustainability in filtration? The answer is IDASONIC.

Since 2016, IDASONIC has been offering reliable solutions across a wide spectrum, from academic research to industrial production, with ultrasonic coating, electrospinning nanofiber production, syringe pump, and ultrasonic nozzle technologies.

Our Solutions:

Fuel Cells: Up to 20% efficiency improvement

Medical Devices: Precise drug release in stent coatings

Filtration: High-performance nanofiber-based membranes

Laboratory Solutions: Accurate flow control for microfluidics and R&D processes

What sets IDASONIC apart?

Active distributor network in Europe, Asia and Africa.

Modular and scalable systems

Compliance with ISO and global quality standards

Full technology support from R&D to production

With a global vision, we export nanotechnology solutions to the world.

Contact us: 
www.idasonic.com
info@idasonic.com

Name: Quorum Technologies Limited
Description:
Quorum Technologies manufactures market-leading scientific instruments used for Electron Microscopy (EM) sample preparation.

Electron Microscopy is an essential research tool in many areas of scientific study, from the fight against major diseases, through to food safety and the development of advanced microelectronics and new materials.

At Quorum Technologies we understand that exacting EM sample preparation is the only way to provide our customers with clear imagery for analysis. Leading the way in sample preparation techniques such as cryo-SEM, sputter coating, critical point drying and glow discharge, Quorum Technologies’ full range of high-quality instruments offer unparalleled ease of use and reproducibility – time and time again.

While Quorum Technologies was founded in 2001, our history goes back further to the pioneering EM sample preparation work of Polaron and Emitech. Today Quorum Technologies, a member of Judges Scientific Plc, continues this fine tradition as a trusted partner around the world, selling directly in the UK and with an extensive global network of distributors. 

If you would like to talk to a member of our sales team in the UK please call us on +44(0)1323 810981 or email sales@quorumtech.com.

Name: DELTA-XERO
Description: Delta-Xero is your ideal solution for fluid conditioning. This is made possible by offering thoughtfully designed patented filtration products and solutions to remove varnish and nanoparticulate. We help you contribute to global environmental protection by decreasing waste oil and converting your system fluid to an asset to be valued. We strive to offer our clients exceptional service, added value products and most importantly we provide positive results.

Name: SPARTA Biodiscovery
Description: SPARTA Biodiscovery is a spin-out company from Imperial College London developing and commercialising the SPARTA technology. SPARTA (Single Particle Automated Raman Trapping Analysis) is a breakthrough analytical technology for automated, label-free comprehensive characterisation of nanoformulations. SPARTA is available now as benchtop instrument with powerful in-house developed software packages to get the most out of your data. Enquire now through our website to set up a discovery call!

Name: Quantum Base
Description:
Quantum Base is a world leader in the field of Quantum Security. Driven by excellence in quantum scientific discovery and its commercial application to global security issues, we invent, design, and develop mass producible quantum security solutions and devices at the nanoscale. These are based on quantum mechanics rather than mathematical complexity, so ensuring 100% secure digital information.

We provide simple, practical, scalable quantum security devices that can fit onto any surface or within any electronic device, and are committed to empowering governments, national and global businesses, plus the individuals they serve, to have 100% guaranteed quantum level security and integrity in every data solution they use, and on every product they manufacture, sell and buy.

Name: CMG Technologies MIM and 3D Metal Printing Specialists
Description:
CMG Technologies (previously trading as Egide UK) is an internationally renowned specialist in Metal Injection Moulding (MIM), providing injection moulded components to the medical, aerospace and industrial sectors for over 14 years. 

Our expert team of senior engineers have over 25 years’ experience in industry and are able to facilitate the entire MIM process in house - from tool design and build, to compounding the feedstock, through to the final sintering stage. This tight control at all stages ensures components are produced to a consistent quality and in line with the full accreditation ISO9001:2015. 

In summary, MIM combines the design freedom and ease of plastic injection moulding with the performance of metal, to produce complex, tightly toleranced, high density metal components. 

As an innovative company, CMG Technologies consistently develops the metal injection moulding process and collaborates with a number of industrial partners and universities to further expand its level of knowledge. Current projects include development of new materials and miniaturisation.

Name: Durham Magneto Optics
Description:
Welcome to Durham Magneto Optics Ltd. We specialize in advanced scientific instrumentation for nanotechnology research and development. Our product range includes a family of magneto-optical Kerr effect magnetometers (NanoMOKE3) and a family of direct-write laser lithography machines (MicroWriter ML).

Durham Magneto Optics Ltd was founded in 2002 as a spin-off company from Professor Russell Cowburn’s nanomagnetism research group in Durham University Physics Department. During a decade of successful trading since then, DMO has deployed machines world wide. We have a global network of sales and support staff provided by the well known scientific instrumentation companies Quantum Design and LOT-Oriel.

Name: Institute of Thin Films, Sensors and Imaging (ITFSI)
Description: The Institute of Thin Films, Sensors and Imaging  (ITFSI) is a research institute at the University of the West of Scotland (UWS), founded by Professor Des Gibson in September 2014. ITFSI specialises in thin films for various applications, including medical devices, sensors, engineering, optics, electronic devices, and photonics. A range of thin film technologies, leading to products including miniaturised spectrometers for gas sensing, ultrasonics, hyper-spectral imaging applications, durable infra-red optical coatings, and low thermal noise coatings for gravitational wave mirror coatings.

Name: Moorfield Nanotechnology
Description:
Moorfield — excellence in vacuum technology since 1989.

Moorfield was created to provide services in vacuum technology primarily to the academic research market. While the initial service and retrofit side of the business is still important for ongoing customer communication and feedback, the company has now grown to supply products manufactured in-house.

Our vacuum deposition range is aimed at pilot-scale industrial production and high-end educational institutions. System designs involve extensive modularity, leading to flexible solutions ideal for R&D environments where changing technical requirements are common. The range consists of starter platforms that can then be populated with numerous component sets for deposition of metals, inorganics and organics. Systems can be built as standalone units, or can be combined with gloveboxes when air sensitivity is an issue.

Recently, Moorfield have directed R&D toward chemical vapour deposition (CVD) systems that allow for easy production of the ‘wonder materials’ graphene and carbon nanotubes (CNTs). These developments have attracted government funding and have been aided by consultation with expert academic researchers. The systems are capable of scalable, cost-efficient synthesis of high-quality material through the implementation of growth schemes deemed critical for future commercialisation of carbon nanomaterials.

Moorfield formed the Clean Environments division in 1997 after failing to find a portable clean space in which to get sign-off for its deposition systems. The Clean Environments team have since developed a range of rapid-assembly, low cost, HEPA filtered products for creating portable and permanent cleanroom areas.

Name: Official euspen
Description:
The European Society for Precision Engineering and Nanotechnology (euspen) has a prestigious heritage.  It was formed in 1998 when a group of leading indusrialist and academics came together with a wish to provide a networking forum for this key community, complementary to that which existed in both Japan and the US.

With representation across 32 countries worldwide, euspen provides a technical focus on: 
- ultra/nano-precision manufacturing
- design and build of ultra-precision machine systems
-characterisation; metrology systems, instruments and techniques

euspen today is a highly respected body of outstanding industrialists and researchers.  Together we set the standards for innovation in the field precision, micro and nano engineering.

Join our membership society - www.euspen.eu

Name: HT Materials Science
Description:
HT Materials Science (HTMS) is the global leader in smart heat transfer fluids for commercial and industrial heating and cooling systems. We help any business with a high heating or cooling demand to make significant energy and carbon savings – from commercial offices and data centres through to manufacturers, pharmaceutical & healthcare facilities and more. 

Our patented MaxwellTM product is a drop-in nanofluid additive that’s proven to enhance the heat transfer of a base fluid by more than 15%. It delivers immediate results (with no costly downtime needed), making HVAC systems instantly more efficient and sustainable. 

MaxwellTM can reduce a company’s energy costs by 12-15% or more and can also increase a system’s capacity. This means businesses can get more out of their existing equipment for longer, as their heating or cooling demands increase. Our technology is already being successfully used by a host of major companies across the US, EMEA and Asia, bringing them enhanced efficiencies, cost savings and lower carbon footprints as a result. 

At HTMS we proudly work with some of the best science and engineering minds in the world, with offices in Dublin, Lecce (Italy) and New York. R&D is at the heart of everything we do, and we’re constantly developing future technologies to help businesses reduce energy consumption and their environmental impact.

Name: Mater-AI
Description: At Mater-AI we're using physics-based modelling and AI to speed up the discovery of materials optimised for electrical and thermal properties.

Name: Gencoa Ltd
Accelerated Materials
Description:
Accelerated Materials provides businesses with end-to-end solutions for nanomaterial production. We develop and supply next generation hardware, software and services for materials innovation and manufacturing. We are located in the United Kingdom and Singapore.

It often takes decades to industrialize new material technologies. AM uses a fundamentally different R&D methodology, incorporating intensified microreactor technology and machine learning to accelerate scale-up. We reduce the time and cost to scale high precision materials by up to 90%.

AM was founded to commercialize inventions and know-how developed in various projects at the University of Cambridge and Cambridge Centre for Advanced Research and Education in Singapore (CARES Ltd) since 2015.

Name: Micro Materials Ltd
Description:
Micro Materials Ltd has been supplying high quality nano-mechanical test instruments (nanoindenter and microindenter) to industry and academia since 1988. The company’s instruments offer the market’s most complete range of nano-scale mechanical tests, delivered in the industry’s widest variety of simulated environmental conditions including hot, cold, humid and liquid atmospheres.

The company’s flagship instrument – the NanoTestTM Vantage  - is designed to allow customers to carry out all their tests on one flexible, user-friendly platform.

The Vantage offers the world’s leading high temperature nano-indentation system, nano-fretting, nano-scratch and wear tests and patented high strain rate impact technique.

In detail, the capabilities of the NanoTest Vantage include:
•	Nanoindentation (both quasi-static and dynamic)
•	Nano-impact and fatigue
•	Nano-scratch and wear
•	Nano-fretting
•	Microindentation
•	Micro-scratch
•	High temperature nanoindentation, nanoscratch and nanoimpact to 850 oC
•	Low temperature nanoindentation and nanoscratch to -20 oC
•	Liquid cell
•	Humidity unit

Recently Micro Materials has set an industry precedent with the launch of the NanoTest Xtreme.  This is the world’s first commercial system for carrying out high (and low) temperature nanoindentation measurements under vacuum conditions. 

The Company is known for its dynamic development programme that has led to industry firsts like the high temperature stage and the impact testing module.  The focus of the developments is on providing the researcher with a comprehensive and versatile instrument that allows a wide range of real world operating conditions to be simulated in a practical way.

Based in the UK, Micro Materials Ltd also houses a testing laboratory and demonstration suite.  You are welcome to visit the demonstration suite to gain a full appreciation of the range of techniques and test conditions that are available on the NanoTest Vantage.

Name: NanoSight Ltd
Description:
A wide range of research fields including medical science, medical diagnostics, materials science, environmental protection, and metrology would hugely benefit from better data and knowledge on nanoparticles. To meet this requirement, Nanosight has developed unique and innovative instruments for imaging and measuring individual nanoparticles.

The instruments give data on particle size distribution, concentration, and aggregation, with much higher resolution, sensitivity and accuracy than has been previously possible. The addition of fluorescence and Zeta measurement options dramatically extends the capabilities of the instruments, allowing truly multi-parametric characterisation of nanoparticles.

Endorsed by an exponential growth in scientists citing its use in scientific papers, and applicable in a wide range of fluids, including complex biological systems, the Nanosight system provides scientists with detailed data and knowledge of nanoparticle systems that was previously unavailable.

Name: Smart Nano NI
Description:
Smart Nano NI is a Northern Ireland consortium collaborating to develop game-changing advanced prototyping and smart manufacturing methods to deliver new technologies. The consortium shares a niche capability around nano manufacturing and world-leading knowledge in photonics. The consortium has been awarded £42.4m UK Research and Innovation’s Strength in Places Fund. The total project value including leveraged funding from other sources is £63.9m. Our collaboration is aimed at driving self-sustaining local industry and economic growth through research and innovation. 

The consortium has been awarded seedcorn funding of £50,000 to develop their bid and compete for a share of £236m from the UK Research and Innovation’s Strength in Places Fund. Our collaboration is aimed at driving self-sustaining local industry and economic growth through research and innovation.

Name: REWIRE-IKC
Description:
REWIRE connects world-leading semiconductor research with real-world commercial outcomes - accelerating the development of next-generation power electronics through flexible, low-barrier collaborations across industry and academia. 
We offer access to cutting-edge expertise, facilities, connections, and insight to help partners de-risk innovation, shape the semiconductor roadmap, influence policy and bring breakthrough materials like SiC, GaN, and Ga2O3 closer to market.
We work to translate the next generation of high-voltage wide and ultra-wide bandgap compound semiconductor devices into pioneering technologies - delivering new products to market, driving growth in the UK semiconductor sector, and accelerating the UK’s net-zero ambitions.
REWIRE is an Innovation and Knowledge Centre (IKC) funded by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) and Innovate UK, both part of UK Research and Innovation.  The program is delivered by world-leading academic teams at the Universities of Bristol, Cambridge and Warwick.

Name: Microsaic Systems
Description: We serve Human & Environmental Health with online, at-line and front-line workflows for therapeutics, diagnostics, manufacturing, & environmental epidemiology

Name: Nikalyte Ltd
Description:
Nikalyte Ltd designs and manufactures advanced Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) systems and high-performance Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) substrates for research and industrial applications.

Our deposition techniques include magnetron sputtering, e-beam evaporation, thermal evaporation, and gas condensation, ensuring ultra-pure, well-controlled deposition processes for advanced battery and energy materials, electrochemistry and catalysis, quantum materials, and sensing applications.

In parallel, our gold and silver SERS substrates deliver reliable, high-sensitivity detection for chemical, biological, environmental, pharmaceutical, food safety, and forensic analysis.

With deep expertise in vacuum engineering and SERS, Nikalyte supports universities, R&D laboratories, and technology innovators worldwide.

Name: NuNano
Description:
NuNano is a UK-based company specialising in the design and manufacture of probes for atomic force microscopy and cantilever-based sensor devices. Building on over 30 years of experience in atomic force microscopy, proprietary microfabrication processes enable NuNano to manufacture AFM probes with the tightest dimensional tolerances in the market at present. Furthermore, NuNano is passionate about providing AFM users with the best possible customer service, from the first time you visit our website to storing your probes after a successful day on the microscope.
NuNano is always interested in hearing from potential distributors. Please contact us at info@nunano.com.

Name: NANOPLUME
Description: NANOPLUME is a US- and UK-based advanced biomaterials company, scaling the manufacture of the world's lightest, thinnest, and best insulating material - Bio-Aerogel. NANOPLUME's technology reduces costs by 75%, making the super-insulating biomaterial accessible to the built environment and other industries, dramatically increasing energy efficiency, space efficiency, and circularity.

Name: Bristol Nano Dynamics
Description:
Our innovative video-rate scanning probe microscope images cm2 areas with nanometre resolution and can track dynamic processes in real time. The product of 10 years of intensive development, our technology is fundamentally different from traditional atomic force microscopes but produces images and data with similar resolution and accuracy to the best competing high-speed AFMs in only a 1,000th of the time!

Creative researchers are already using our instruments to carry out analyses that were previously thought impossible across diverse fields from genomics to 2D materials, batteries and semiconductors.

We continue to develop new technologies and will be launching a scanning probe (patent pending) version of our microscope soon for semiconductor wafer measurements.

Contact us for more details and a demonstration on your own samples.

Name: Institute of Nanotechnology
Description:
About the Institute...

Our Vision:
"To be the foremost global nanotechnology information provider and membership organisation."

Our Mission:
"To foster, develop and promote all aspects of responsible nanoscience and nanotechnology that have the potential to benefit society and the environment"

Background:
The Institute of Nanotechnology (IoN) was founded by Ottilia Saxl in January 1997. It is a registered Charity, whose core activities are focused on education and training in nanotechnology. It grew out of the Centre for Nanotechnology, part funded by the DTI through the UK 's National Initiative on Nanotechnology (NION). The Institute was one of the world's first nanotechnology information providers and is now a global leader.

The Institute works closely with governments, universities, researchers, companies and the general public to educate and inform on all aspects of nanotechnology. It also organises various international scientific events, conferences and educational courses that examine the implications of nanotechnology for industry, society, health, energy and the environment, and the disadvantaged communities across the globe.

Name: Loughborough Materials Characterisation Centre (LMCC)
Description:
Loughborough Materials Characterisation Centre (LMCC) is located within the Materials Department of Loughborough University. The Centre’s primary aim is to support materials research within the Materials Department and the University as a whole. However, supporting industry by providing specialist services is also seen as a very important part of LMCC’s activities.

Loughborough Materials Characterisation Centre provide a wide range of analytical services for industrial clients on all of our instruments. The centre has a wealth of experience in conducting consultancy projects and has dedicated staff to ensure projects can be delivered on time.

Name: Oxford nanoSystems
Description: OnS supplies advanced test stations and equipment for water electrolyser and materials innovation.  Our two platforms (ElectroFlow(TM) ETS 5 and 100) are used across academia, SMEs and large corporates.  Bespoke test station and equipment can also be supplied.

Name: Microsol
Description:
Simulate | Formulate | Deliver. 

Microsol de-risks and accelerates the development of orally and nasally inhaled drug products.

The formulation design space is vast, and empirical exploration consumes scarce API and limited lab time.

We help you spend your bench time on the experiments that matter.

Our platform pairs proprietary single-particle measurement with physics-based simulation and machine learning to narrow the design space before you commit to the bench, so your experiments are fewer, better chosen, and provide the insights needed. You spend your API where it counts, and you find the problems early.

We work across pMDI, DPI, nebulised and nasal systems, including inhaled biologics, where the formulation window is narrowest and the need is greatest.

Name: Cambridge Nanomaterials Technology Ltd
Description:
The Cambridge Nanomaterials Technology (CNT) Ltd is innovation management consultancy company based in Cambridge, England with expertise in technology innovation and development of products enhanced with application of nanomaterials (nanotubes and nanowires, graphene and other 2D nanomaterials and nanoparticles). Please visit our virtual exhibition and community development website: www.nanoMATexpo.net 
The CNT Ltd helps companies, academic and government institutions to develop innovation including R&D and IP strategy, strategic technology development and investment partnership, products, technologies and market. The CNT Ltd is specialised in innovation consulting for clients in industry, academia and government agencies and collaborative R&D project management and exploitation and dissemination management in government funded projects  such as European Horizon 2020 and UK Government Innovate UK funded projects. CNT team is actively involved supporting project consortium building and proposal preparation and project management.

Name: RAB-Microfluidics
Description:
RAB-Microfluidics is a Research & Development company developing cutting-edge microfluidic technology to solve oil analysis problems.

For too long, stationary laboratories have been the way to test and analyse oil samples, however, oil analysis does not have to be static and one dimensional. We believe this process should be dynamic like everything else around us, that’s why we are revolutionising oil testing and analysis services by making conventional laboratory procedures mobile, rapid and routine. Our innovation is driven by the needs of our customers in oil & gas, aerospace & defence, processing & manufacturing, power generation, transport and maritime industries.

Our microfluidic technology invention is the product of a decade-long research from world recognised college of Physical Science at the University of Aberdeen. RAB-Microfluidics is strategically located at the heart of this citadel of technological expertise, being the pioneering developer of microfluidic technology for oil applications in Europe. We have unparalleled world class expertise in development of microfluidic technology at out behest working with award winning product development partners in the United Kingdom. Our advisory team has over 60 years’ worth of experience and expertise in knowledge underpinning our technology, business development and commercialisation.

Name: Future Textiles
Description: Sustainable Materials for Wearable E-textiles

Name: RESPILON
Description:
Our mission from 2013:
- to protect human health using modern technology
- to commercialize products from Czech nanofibers
- to launch high-grade nanofiber products to the market

Our vision
We want to become a worldwide leading supplier of nanofiber material & products and thus allow to people to experience their benefits & features in everyday life.

What is RESPILON?
- material with huge potential and completely different qualities compared to traditional materials
- nanotechnology, thanks to which many people will avoid infections and people suffering from allergies can breathe freely
- nanofiber membrane used in the ReSpimask, Respilon AIR or Night Care
- thanks to RESPILON, you can already make use of nanotechnology every day and enjoy its benefits

Name: Peratech Holdco Limited
Description:
NO LONGER TRADING – Peratech is a pressure-sensing solutions company with our patented QTC technology that provides cost-effective, mass-produced next-generation touch solutions to some of the most exciting and innovative companies in mobile, automotive, industrial, robotics, electronic appliance, consumer electronics, and health/sport diagnostics markets. 

We are an award-winning team of passionate technologists, engineers, scientists, and problem solvers looking for the best fellow teammates to help make our company a great success.  We are an equal opportunity employer that believes the best people come from all walks of life all over the world.

Name: NANOSMAT
Description: NANOSMAT conferences are designed to provide an effective and stimulating platform for international people to foster, develop and promote communication, education, networking, dissemination of knowledge, research and innovations in all aspects of nanoscience and nanotechnology.

Name: Particle Works now part of Unchained Labs
Description: Particle Works is now part of Unchained Labs.  We design and build game-changing particle engineering platforms that allow scientists to take complete control of their nanoparticle production process.  Please follow Unchained Labs for all future information.  This page will be closing shortly.

Name: Smart Separations Ltd
Description:
Smart Separations is a limited company based in London UK (Founded in 2013, Company no. 08600897). It has patented an innovative microfiltration (MF) technology to produce ceramic filters with self-assembled controllable pores of uniform size in the range between <1 and 50μm. This tight pore size control and range availability will revolutionise the field of MF with a cost-effective product. Our ambition is to be the world’s leader in MF and particle separations technology – filling the void gap that exists in the market nowadays.

Our mission? “Improve quality of life through innovation”,  in the areas of health, the environment and human causes.

Name: CN Technical Services Ltd
Description:
Trusted Distributors of Industry Leading Scientific Instrumentation.

CN Tech specialises in Metrology Instrumentation, Mechanical and Tribological Testing, Electron Microscopy, Surface Analysis, Environmental Isolation, Gloveboxes, Sample Preparation, and Laboratory Equipment and Consumables.

Founded in 2009, CN Tech’s focused and experienced team is dedicated to finding the right solution for customers in UK and beyond. With many years of experience in the fields of metrology and nanoscience, our technical specialists can help provide imaging and measurement solutions for a wide range of academic and industrial needs.

We pride ourselves in providing a complete package of analysis and testing solutions. Whatever the application, our skilled engineers can offer new insight in imaging and metrology.

Name: Carbon Air
Description:
Carbon Air’s patented application of activated carbon technology to automotive, mobility and other sectors enables a specific control and tune of the behaviour of air. 

From vehicle air springs and gas-charged dampers, to air springs in commercial vehicle seats, and mountain bike forks and shocks, Carbon Air enables enhanced performance in a more compact package. 

Find out more about our technology on at http://carbonair.eu/

Name: Functional Materials and Energy Devices Research Group
Description: The Functional Materials and Energy Devices group (FMED) led by Dr Mojtaba Abdi-Jalebi researches the discovery of novel energy materials and advanced energy devices based on low-temperature processable molecular semiconductors and hybrid organic-inorganic heterostructures between such organic semiconductors and inorganic semiconductors, such as metal halide perovskites, metal oxides and nanoparticles. These functional materials are of growing interest for a range of emerging technological applications, including low-cost, large area photovoltaics, energy-efficient light-emitters, electrochemical devices and other energy applications and flexible electronics. Our research aims to discover and incorporate new inexpensive functional materials in energy devices to alter the energy landscape by reducing the cost of energy production, consumption, and storage.

Name: Resysten International Ltd
Description:
Resysten Hungary Ltd. was established in 2014 with the aim of providing advanced, scientifically validated solutions for long-term surface hygiene protection. Our founders envisioned a technology that is highly effective, sustainable, and capable of creating measurable benefits for both public health and the environmental objectives over the long term.

Today, Resysten operates across multiple continents and serves a wide range of industries. Our technologies are used worldwide by transportation companies, healthcare institutions, industrial operators and corporate environments. What we offer is not merely a coating or a technology, but a complete,professionally managed service with full implementation.

Our hygiene protection coating provides durable, 24/7 active protection against viruses, bacteria, fungi and mold. The solution is particularly effective in high-traffic, shared environments—such as public transport, offices, healthcare facilities and schools—where infection risks are elevated. Beyond its hygiene benefits, the technology also delivers measurable economic value by reducing cross-contamination and lowering absenteeism.

The Resysten Clean Air photocatalytic coating is specifically designed for city environments. It effectively breaks down airborne nitrogen oxides (NOx) and other pollutants, contributing to improved air quality. It is an ideal solution for building facades, bus stops, underpasses and other high-traffic urban locations.

Resysten’s mission remains unchanged: to develop innovative, sustainable solutions that measurably improve environmental and human health—from everyday touch surfaces to the the air we breathe.

Name: G24 Power
Description: GCell is the brand leader in the design, manufacture and introduction of disruptive technologies for use in portable consumer electronics, wireless sensing and autonomous beaconing devices. GCell is making disposable batteries obsolete with the use of energy harvesting, ultra-low power electronics and hybrid energy solutions. GCell’s commitment to innovation in autonomous ambient intelligence gives users the freedom to disconnect from mains power and not be restricted by the limitations of batteries.

Name: Poradigm Technologies
Description:
Poradigm is developing the fluid platform for precision chemical separations.

Our technology is based on porous liquids, a new class of materials that combine the molecular precision of porous solids with the flexibility and process advantages of liquids. This enables new approaches to separation that can reduce energy demand, improve selectivity, and unlock process designs that are not possible with conventional technologies.

We focus on the full pathway from molecular design to engineered systems. This includes materials discovery, formulation, pilot scale testing, and process integration. Our modular test infrastructure and data driven development approach allow us to generate credible performance data and accelerate the transition from concept to deployment.

Poradigm works with industrial partners across energy, chemicals, and advanced manufacturing to solve complex separation challenges. Our goal is to deliver practical, scalable solutions that create measurable performance and economic advantage.

We are building a new class of separation technology designed for flexibility, tuneability, and real world operation.

Name: OXGRIN (Oxford Green Innotech)
Description:
Pioneering Zero-Carbon Ammonia-Powered Solutions for a Sustainable Future

Spin-out company backed by the University of Oxford

Name: Aavalor
Description:
Aavalor Greentech builds ceramic-graphene hybrid membranes that recover 80–90% of cooling water at ≤1 bar, while conventional systems grind away at ~10 to 20 bar.

The result: 7 to 10× less energy, 50% more throughput, and removal of PFAS, nitrates, phosphates and COD, validated on real cooling water at WaterCampus Leeuwarden. For a typical data centre or power plant, that can translate into hundreds of thousands of euros in annual savings and hundreds of millions of litres of water kept in supply.
From crisis to breakthrough: empowering the future of industrial cooling water. Building the hardware every data center and power plant needs.

Name: Silson
Description: We manufacture specialist consumables and components for x-ray microscopy, electron microscopy, accelerator mass spectrometry and related fields. We specialise in the manufacture of ultra-thin membranes and related micro and nanotechnologies. We hold thousands of membranes in stock, which are available for immediate delivery. Feel free to drop us a message if you have any questions or if you'd like to make an enquiry!

Name: Stream Bio
Description: We design, develop & manufacture revolutionary products based on our unique & super stable Conjugated Polymer Nanoparticles, up to 1000x brighter than QDots. #DiscoverBright

Name: planarTECH
Description: Headquartered in Cambridge, UK and with its manufacturing base in Korea, planarTECH aims to enable graphene, carbon nanotube (CNT), and 2D material applications development by providing researchers worldwide with high-quality equipment for materials synthesis and characterization. In addition to its core competency in 2D materials, planarTECH also has years of experience in manufacturing high-quality vacuum systems and components. With a global network of researchers at leading institutions in Asia, the US and Europe, planarTECH has assembled the process know-how to assist customers in starting their research program as quickly as possible.

Name: NanoPrint Innovations Limited
Description: Deep-tech startup working on next generation thin film deposition systems and engineering of functional oxide coatings for photovoltaic applications

Name: LiquidNano Inc
Description: LiquidNano is using the latest Nano-Technology to develop protective coatings for a variety of consumer and commercial uses.  We are at the forefront of this exciting technology using inert, mineral based liquid-glass to give sector-leading performance with zero environmental impact.

Name: Henniker Scientific Ltd.
Description:
Henniker – Passionate about Plasma

Plasma Treatment - Plasma Cleaners, Plasma Etchers, Plasma Coating & Plasma Surface Modification

We are a leading manufacturer of plasma treatment systems for cleaning, surface activation to improve adhesion, and functional nano-scale coating.

Our innovative plasma treatment equipment is trusted globally in both critical industrial manufacturing settings and by leading academic research groups where it is used in biomedical research, life sciences, energy storage, filtration and many other areas of materials science in general.

Visit our website for more information on the following areas of plasma technology:-

Plasma Technology

Learn more about the science and technology of plasma surface treatment and surface energy.

Plasma Treatments

Comprehensive details and application examples to help you find the right plasma system.

Products & Services

Our full range of plasma surface treatment products and our range of surface treatment methods.

Industry Sectors

Industry specific plasma treatment solutions, including example processes and applications.

Test & Development 

We operate extensive laboratory facilities to assess, test and investigate all aspects of plasma surface modification on a wide range of materials.
Coupled with extensive in-house and real-world knowledge, we can deliver a tailored treatment to suit your individual product or production needs quickly and efficiently.

Visit our website ‘Knowledge Base’ 
Everything you need to understand plasma technology all in one place.

Knowledge Articles – discover more with application notes and cutting edge research enabled by our plasma treatment systems and processes

Videos – View our explainer videos for more information on plasma treatment technology

Case Studies – Review our case studies developed alongside our customers and including real world processes and results.

Name: Plasma Quest
Description: Plasma Quest Ltd is a solutions provider for thin film sputter-deposition specialising in a unique plasma generation process that enables high rate, exceptional quality coatings of many different materials at ambient temperatures. PQL has developed a variety of deposition tools suitable for a wide range of end user applications from small R&D through to large area, high throughput coatings. The recently enhanced linear deposition process is capable of highly uniform coatings over a 14 inch web. The exclusive technique enables an array of new applications, materials and substrates. A key example of the exceptional attributes of the process is the low temperature deposition of indium tin oxide that has a sheet resistance of less than 10Ω/o with >97% peak transmission. Furthermore, the ITO is well adhered to a variety of substrates including planarised PEN and PET substrates and can be repeatedly flexed with a bend radius of <1cm whilst demonstrating no reduction in conductivity. Other materials deposited at ambient temperatures include a wide range of high breakdown dielectrics with 100% peak transmission and high mobility (>20cm2/Vs) transparent semiconductors suitable for flexible electronics applications. PQL offers a complete range of services from contract R&D through to complete bespoke deposition systems.

Name: DCN Corp
Description:
Designing & Manufacturing Equitable NanoTech solutions 

At DCN Corp we hope to transform Nano-Tech into accessible and life-enhancing diagnostic platform technologies.

Our proprietary platform technology is validated to TRL 3, and protected by a robust hybrid IP strategy.

- What We Do:
We’ve developed a useful Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) process technology, designed for next-gen diagnostics.

It enables:
- Real-time biological insights
- Quantitative severity analysis
- Compatibility with Raman & Infrared instruments

This innovation should evolve into a scalable handheld bio-kit for early detection and precision diagnostics.

- Our Mission:
To pioneer Nano-tech applications that positively impact humanity. Through rigorous science and inclusive design, we aim to democratise diagnostics for global health equity.

- Our Vision:
We all know someone affected by cancer, cardiovascular disease, or other life-altering conditions. These illnesses respond better to early and accurate detection. Therefore, our vision is to create a handheld diagnostic bio-kit that supports this goal - aligned with future at-home diagnostics requirements.

Supported by research - Crosby et al. (2022), Science Journal: “Early Detection of Cancer”.

- Market & Impact Potential:
- Global diagnostics market: £140B+
- SPR-based tools projected to grow 9.40% CAGR (up to 2032)
- Early detection improves survival rates by up to 70%

- What We’re Looking For:
To bring this vision to life, we’re actively seeking:
- R&D & Technical collaborations
- Financial partnerships
- Design & Engineering support
- Next Milestone: Applying Nano-tech to plastic polymer plates to increase bio-sensitivity.
- Fundraising Now: Seed round of £750k+ ($1M+)

Name: NanoLayr UK Ltd
Description:
NanoLayr UK Ltd is the UK subsidiary of NanoLayr Ltd, an industry-leading nanofibre R&D, customisation and manufacturing company. Through our in-house developed concept to product electrospinning platform, we can provide our clients with a full proof-of-concept to prototype to commercial manufacturing solution. 
NanoLayr UK (formally Radical Fibres Ltd) was founded in October 2019 to address the market need for modern high-performance materials in this market, bringing new horizons with nanofibre technology to the UK, before being acquired by world nanofibre leaders NanoLayr Ltd (New Zealand) in 2022. Our team of nanofibre experts work in bespoke, inhouse built labs to tailor these materials to meet customer needs in a manner which translates straight through to large area manufacturing at NanoLayr’s Auckland facility. 
Nanofibres are rapidly proving to be the solution to countless current challenges, often offering material solutions to problems where low weights and high performances are key. Our current product speciality areas include, but not limited to, rapid dermal delivery platforms, smart textile sensors, high performance filter media, composite toughening veils, acoustic attenuation, and biodegradable alternatives.

Name: LIG Nanowise Ltd
Description:
LIG Nanowise is a Manchester based scientific instruments company founded in 2014, developing world leading product offerings in microscopy and nanopatterning. We apply microsphere lens technology to diverse applications from imaging to industrial manufacturing. Microspheres will become a super material at the heart of some of the most important innovations in the optics space.

We developed the world’s most powerful brightfield microscope; the NANORO M, which can achieve 50 nm resolutions purely through glass and light. This utilises SMAL (Super-resolution Microsphere Amplifying Lens) technology to provide new insights into nanostructures - non-destructively, in full colour, rapidly and with no sample preparation. This has major applications in materials science research, microelectronics and 2D materials imaging. We launched this product in June 2017 through our imaging brand NANORO to international media aclaim.

We are also developing a best in class particle lens array that can produce nanoscale patterns rapidly and repeatably with high precision over a wide area, with applications in microfluidics, semiconductors and bank note security.

For enquires, please contact us:

0161 342 0515

Company Website: www.lig-nanowise.com

Twitter: https://twitter.com/LIGNanowise

Description: Nanosynth Group PLC specialises in the synthesis and application of nanoparticles to create new and existing products

Name: Nanoscale Energy and Surface Engineering
Description:
We are a Nanoscale Energy research team based at University of Surrey and The Open University, UK, led by Prof Satheesh Krishnamurthy, Director of Surrey Ion Beam Centre. Our research is socially oriented, technologically transformational and has a direct impact on society. 

Our laboratory is involved in the research of advanced nanomaterials with these specific application areas:

 • Alternative energy, 
 • Multifunctional nanocomposites, 
 • Additive manufacturing
 • Wastewater treatment 

Our research focuses on materials science and engineering technologies that will impact our society in the future. 

Our group is committed to changing the world through discoveries and the development of new materials and technologies that will have a direct impact on society. 

Our efforts begin where the igniting and imaginative mind meets the experienced. We are excited about what future technology can offer societal wellbeing and aspire to be leading players in this endeavour, becoming missionaries of science in our lifetime.

Name: Ultrafilter G.Britain Ltd
Description:
The Ultrafilter group is a privately owned family company. Founded by Dipl. Ing. Dean Kronsbein in Germany, the group now serves the global filtration market with local presence throughout Europe, The Americas, Asia and Australia.

With the help of our products from ultrafilter GmbH in Germany, world renowned, market leading companies have made ultrafilter GmbH their first choice for the Purification of compressed air, technical gases and liquids.
Our passion to manufacture superior and innovative products is the guarantee for cost effective and reliable filtration solutions.

Compressed air, we can offer many different kinds of compressed air filters that are compatible with compressed air systems of all brands. We also offer compressed air dryers, adsorption and membrane dryers in addition to auto drain compressors, compressed air tanks and oil-water separators. Additionally, we have a sterile, compressed air filter for food and beverage applications.

Liquid filtration, we offer all kinds of filters for liquids such as bag filters, absolute filters and membrane filters, for industrial applications, such as coolant. We have a great deal of experience with filter solutions for the food and beverage industry, and our products are approved by EC 1935/2004 as well as FDA. We also have filters for drinking water.

Gas filtration, we have leading generator technology for manufacturing nitrogen and oxygen, and for filtering all kinds of gas like methane and bio gas.

Name: SAFENANO
Description:
Established as a Centre of Excellence in Nanosafety in 2006 at the UK’s Institute of Occupational Medicine (IOM), SAFENANO provides industry, academia and governments with independent authoritative expertise and state-of-the-art facilities to enable effective risk management.

We bring together multidisciplinary expertise in hazard assessment, exposure, toxicology, occupational hygiene and risk assessment, facilitating the responsible development of nanomaterials and nanotechnology-enabled products by making use of an integrated approach combining research, review activities, expert opinion and best practice training.

These services are supported by a free-to-access Knowledge Base, focusing on interpreting and transferring the emerging scientific evidence about the potential risks to health and the environment arising from the development and use of nanotechnology.

Effective risk management protects your business and gives you confidence in developing and realising the potential of nanotechnology by:
- maintaining investor, workforce and consumer trust;
- guarding against potential future liabilities and prosecution;
- protecting your reputation and brand.  

With global coverage from our UK and Singapore offices, IOM has unrivalled expertise and capability in risk management designed to support research, regulation, and commercialisation of nanotechnology.  With unparalleled expertise, facilities and services, there is no one better placed to help you manage the increasingly complex risk presented to your business.

For further information, please visit our website http://www.safenano.org

Name: Centre for Programmable Biological Matter
Description:
At the Centre for Programmable Biological Matter, we are interested in understanding, designing and building natural and artificial bionanomachines.

Bionanomachines are fascinating nanoscale machines made from biological molecules, typically proteins, lipids, RNA and DNA. In nature they carry out an amazing array of tasks, from copying our DNA to converting light into energy. 

We use a mixture of biochemical, structural and computational techniques plus the most important ingredient: imagination. 

Currently we are particularly interested in the natural machine DNA gyrase both because of its fascinating and intricate mechanism but also because it is an important target for development of new antibacterial drugs.

We are also building artificial structures from proteins and DNA with the aim of developing Programmable Biological Matter. This describes artificial nanoscale biological material which can be programmed to move on demand. This will be useful for new materials and particularly medical use for example in effective vaccines and smart drug delivery systems which may one day be used as effective disease treatments in particular for age-associated diseases.

Funded by The Leverhulme Trust and Academy of Medical Sciences.

Name: CALIN - Celtic Advanced Life Science Innovation Network
Description:
Celtic Advanced Life Science Innovation Network (CALIN): bringing together business, academic and clinical excellence to encourage growth and innovation across the life science sector in Ireland & Wales.
